subject: Clarify billing for streaming timeouts and proration - Acme Health
messages:
From: John Peterson <john.peterson@acmehealth.com>
To: alex_martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 11:12:00 -0500
Subject: Strange charges after our load test (streaming sessions)

Alex —

We ran a week-long load test against the hosted streaming endpoint and our finance team noticed a number of unexpected token charges for sessions that were terminated by gateway timeouts. The attached load-test-session-log.zip has a couple hundred examples where the client got "HTTP/1.1 524 A Timeout Occurred" but our client SDK had already received partial chunks.

Two quick questions: can you explain Redwood's billing boundary for streaming sessions (is billing based on tokens generated by the model or tokens ACKed/delivered to the client?), and is there any standard proration/credit policy for mass transient disconnects caused by a downstream network?

We have a term sheet review next week and need to understand how these events could affect our baseline spend.

Thanks,
John Peterson
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Health

---
Attachments: load-test-session-log.zip (zip)

From: alex.martinez@redwood.com <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: John Peterson <john.peterson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: rachel.kim@redwood.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 11:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Strange charges after our load test (streaming sessions)

John —

Thanks for sending the logs. I'm looping in Rachel (pricing) and Stephanie (billing ops) so we can give you a precise account of what happened and options on credits/proration. High level answers up front:

- Billing boundary: for streaming responses we meter tokens at generation time on the serving runtime. That means when a token is emitted by the model backend it can be counted even if the HTTP stream is interrupted before the client receives the final bytes. However, we also track delivery and have policies for reconnect/retry situations.
- Short disconnects: we have a 45-second "resume window" for sessions using the same session id/idempotency key where we will attempt to stitch the KV cache; if the session resumes within that window we do not double-bill for overlapping token ranges.
- Gateway timeouts and large-scale network failures: we don't automatically credit every timeout. We evaluate on a case-by-case basis for infra incidents. That said, for load-test storms that clearly originated upstream (your LB or region network), we can provide a one-time goodwill credit while we jointly investigate.

Can you confirm how your client is generating session ids and whether you used idempotency keys across retries? If you can share a short sample (or point to a sample in the logs) showing a broken stream with two close timestamps, that helps our reconciliation.

I'll pick this up with our billing ops and get back with an initial reconciliation and a proposal for a one-time adjustment before your contract review.

—Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: rachel.kim@redwood.com <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: John Peterson <john.peterson@acmehealth.com>, alex.martinez@redwood.com
Cc: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Strange charges after our load test (streaming sessions)

John —

I pulled a sample of affected sessions from your supplied bundle. Observations:

1) ~68% of the chargeable sessions show token events emitted in the backend log followed by a client-side connection close within 3–10s (typical of downstream gateway 502/524).
2) ~22% look like duplicate attempts where the client retried with a new session id (no idempotency key). In those cases we charged for both attempts because the second attempt triggered its own generation steps.
3) ~10% appear to be legitimate long-running generation completions and were delivered successfully.

Our reconciliation approach and options:
- If you can re-run the test with idempotency keys or session-sticky ids (same session id for retries), most of the duplicate-charge noise will disappear because our resume-stitch logic will stitch and de-duplicate token ranges.
- For the immediate invoice, we propose a one-time manual credit covering sessions where (a) you have a backend error code tied to our ingress (we'll provide the matching request ids), and (b) the client did not retry with the same session id within the 45s resume window.

I'm attaching a short spreadsheet with the proposed credit line items (proposed-credit-summary.xlsx). If you prefer an automated protection, we can add a "streaming-grace-window" flag to your account that (for a small premium) will withhold billing for 60s of generated-but-not-delivered tokens pending reconnection. That may be useful for load-test or bursty LB behavior.

Rachel Kim
Pricing Lead | Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: proposed-credit-summary.xlsx (xlsx)

From: John Peterson <john.peterson@acmehealth.com>
To: alex.martinez@redwood.com, rachel.kim@redwood.com
Cc: Acme Health Finance <finance@acmehealth.com>, ops@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 10:33:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Strange charges after our load test (streaming sessions)

Thanks Rachel — the breakdown is helpful. A few follow-ups from our procurement/finance team:

- Can you confirm whether the proposed one-time manual credit will be applied to our upcoming November invoice or as a post-invoice adjustment? Finance prefers invoice-line credits rather than separate refunds.
- How does the "streaming-grace-window" premium get priced? We are evaluating a baseline committed monthly usage and want to understand the delta for that protection.
- Separate ask: in the term sheet we had a line for a 15% baseline hosted-API discount if we commit to 3x baseline usage. Are the credits you described additive to that discount or treated separately?

Our procurement lead (cc'd) will need documented answers for the SOW review.

John

From: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: John Peterson <john.peterson@acmehealth.com>, alex.martinez@redwood.com, rachel.kim@redwood.com
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Strange charges after our load test (streaming sessions)

John —

Answering the procurement questions from the billing ops side:

1) Credit mechanics: we will issue the agreed one-time adjustment as an invoice credit on the November invoice if the reconciliation completes before the invoice cut. If reconciliation completes after the cut we'll post an invoice credit on the next billing cycle (this is standard). We'll flag this as an "investigation adjustment" on the invoice line for your finance team.

2) Streaming-grace-window pricing: the feature is an account-level protection that delays final billing for up to 60s for generated tokens while waiting for reconnection. Pricing examples: for accounts on hosted rate card, the add-on is 3.5% of monthly metered spend (subject to minimum $1,000/mo) for mid-sized customers. For committed contracts (like your proposed 3x baseline), we can offer a negotiated rate — typically we discount the add-on by 25% off list. If you'd like I can model this in the deal worksheet with your expected usage profile.

3) Discounts stacking: credits from operational reconciliation (one-time manual credits) are treated separately from contractual committed-use discounts. The committed-use discount reduces your per-token unit price; the one-time credit will be applied as an invoice line item and does not change unit pricing. The streaming-grace-window add-on is priced on top of the discounted rates, but again we typically offer a bundle discount when the add-on is committed with Reserved capacity or multi-year deals.

Next steps: Marcus will run a reconciliation job and provide a CSV of request ids we propose to credit. If you approve, we'll issue an invoice credit and apply the streaming-grace-window credit toward your negotiation as an optional add-on with the rates above.

—Stephanie Nguyen
Billing Operations Manager | Redwood Inference

On behalf of Marcus Lin (Finance)
